Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:10:1.hebrew: עד שיפרט לך הכתוב - דמדאיצטריך לפרש בנבילה ״לגר אשר בשעריך תתננה ואכלה״ למשרייה בהנאה, ולא נכתב בו אלא ״לא תאכלו״ — ש"מ ״לא תאכלו״ איסור הנאה הוא. ובפסחים (דף כב.) פרכינן עלה טובא. ״לגר בנתינה ולעובד כוכבים במכירה״ — ל"ג במילתיה דרבי אבהו; דאי הוה סבירא ליה ״דברים ככתבן״ דוקא, תו לא מצי יליף מיניה דהיכא דלא פרט היתר ליתסר, דהאי דנבלה לאו אתא להיתר הנאה, אלא לאשמועינן דחילופא אסור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:10:1.english: Unless the verse specifies for you - Since it was necessary to specify regarding an [unslaughtered] carcass: “You may give it to the resident alien who is within your gates, that he may eat it” (Deuteronomy 14:21), to permit deriving benefit from it, and nothing was written regarding it other than “You shall not eat” — learn from this that “you shall not eat” is a prohibition against deriving benefit. And in Pesachim (22a), we raise many difficulties against it. [The phrase:] “To a resident alien by giving and to an idolater by selling” is not our reading in the statement of Rabbi Abbahu; for if he maintained that the words are strictly as written, he could no longer derive from it that wherever [the verse] did not specify permission, it is prohibited, since this [specification] regarding a carcass did not come to permit deriving benefit, but rather to teach us that the reverse is prohibited.

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:11:1.hebrew: ה"מ - דשמעינן איסור הנאה מלשון אכילה היכא דנפקא לן איסור אכילה מיניה, דכיון דמבעי ליה נמי לאזהורי אאכילה, כלל כל הנאות בלשון אכילה — דילפינן מנבילה התם ד"לא יאכל" איסור הנאה נמי משמע. אבל הכא, דאיסור אכילה מקרא אחרינא נפיק, ולא הוצרך זה אלא להנאה — למה לי לאפוקי הנאה בלשון אכילה? ליכתוב "לא יהנה"! אלא ודאי, לאכילה גופיה איצטריך, ולהיכא דשחטיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:11:1.english: This applies only - That we derive a prohibition of benefit from the expression of eating [only] where we derive the prohibition of eating from it. For since it also needed to admonish against eating, it subsumed all [forms of] benefit under the expression of eating, as we derive from a carcass there that “it shall not be eaten” implies a prohibition of benefit as well. But here, where the prohibition of eating is derived from another verse, and this [phrase] was needed only for benefit, why do I need [Scripture] to express benefit using the expression of eating? Let it write: “One may not derive benefit”! Rather, it was certainly needed for eating itself, and for [a case] where one slaughtered it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:12:1.hebrew: אי נמי לכתוב לא יאכל - ולשתוק, את בשרו למה לי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:12:1.english: Alternatively, let [Scripture] write: “It shall not be eaten” - and remain silent; why do I [need] “its flesh”?

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:12:2.english: Like meat - That he slaughtered it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:13:1.hebrew: ואימא ה"מ - דאשמעינן קרא דאפילו שחטו אסור — היכא דבדק צור ושחט בה, דסקילה היא, דמנבלה לא מצי נפיק, דלאו נבלה הוא; אבל שחיטת סכין — לא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:13:1.english: And say [that] these words - That the verse teaches us that even if he slaughtered it, it is forbidden — [apply only] where he inspected a flint and slaughtered with it, for it is [considered] stoning, as it cannot be derived from [the prohibition of] a carcass, since it is not a carcass; but slaughter with a knife [would] not [be forbidden].

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:13:2.hebrew: מידי סכין כתיבא באורייתא - אצל שחיטה? וכיון דהכי הוא, כי שחטה נמי בצור — לאו סקילה היא אלא שחיטה, ואסר לך הכתוב בשרו, והוא הדין סכין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:13:2.english: Was a knife written in the Torah - [in connection] with slaughter? And since that is so, when one slaughters it with a flint as well, it is not stoning but rather slaughter, and Scripture forbade its meat to you; and the same applies to a knife.

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:15:1.english: From where does the hole have [it] - From where does it have the stolen goods?

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:15:2.hebrew: ולהנך תנאי דמפקי ליה להאי ובעל השור נקי - בב"ק (ד' מא:):
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:15:2.english: And according to those tanna’im who expound this [phrase:] “And the owner of the ox shall be clear” - In Bava Kamma (41b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:15:3.hebrew: לחצי כופר - שאם הרג את האדם, נקי מחצי כופר. ואע"ג דמועד משלם כופר שלם, לא אמרינן תם ישלם חצי כופר, כי היכי דגבי נזקין משלם חצי נזק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:15:3.english: For half-ransom - That if [the ox] killed a person, [its owner] is exempt from half-ransom. And even though a forewarned [ox] pays a full ransom, we do not say [that] an innocuous [ox] shall pay half-ransom, just as regarding damages it pays half-damages.

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:15:4.hebrew: ולדמי ולדות - אם נגף אשה הרה ויצאו ילדיה, אינו משלם דמי ולדות לבעל, כמו שהאדם הנוגף משלם, כדכתיב (שמות כא): ענוש יענש וגו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:15:4.english: And for payment for offspring - If [an ox] struck a pregnant woman and her offspring emerged, [the owner] does not pay payment for the offspring to the husband, as a person who strikes [her] pays, as it is written (Exodus 21:22): “He shall surely be punished...”

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:1:1.english: Where he fled - The seller, in whose possession the money is.

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:1:2.hebrew: ומתמהינן: הא לא ברח, קנסינן למוכר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:1:2.english: And we ask in astonishment: But [had] he not fled, we penalize the seller?

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:1:3.hebrew: אלא חורא גנב - אלמלא חור שהעכבר מצניע גניבתו שם, לא היה גונב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:1:3.english: Rather, the hole steals - Were it not for the hole where the mouse hides its stolen goods, it would not steal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:2:1.english: From where does the hole have [it] - From where does it have the stolen goods?

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:3:1.hebrew: המקדש בערלה כו' - דכולהו איסורי הנאה נינהו, כדיליף לה בגמרא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:3:1.english: One who betroths with orla, etc. - For all of them are forbidden from benefit, as [the Gemara] derives in the Gemara:

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:3:2.hebrew: מכרן וקידש בדמיהם מקודשת - דאין הדמים נתפסין באיסור, כדיליף לקמן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:3:2.english: [If] he sold them and betrothed [her] with their proceeds, she is betrothed - For the money does not take on the forbidden status, as [the Gemara] derives later.

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:4:1.english: From where do we [derive it] - That it is forbidden to derive benefit [from it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:4:2.hebrew: מנין שלא יהנה ממנו - כגון שלא יצטבע בו, בפירי הראוי ליצטבע בו, כגון קליפי אגוזין; ושומר לפירי אסור כפירי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:4:2.english: From where [do we derive] that one may not derive benefit from it - For example, that [something] should not be dyed with it, with fruit that is suitable for dyeing with it, such as walnut shells; and a protector of fruit is forbidden like the fruit.

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:4:3.english: And one may not light a lamp with it - For example, from [its] oil.

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:6:1.hebrew: אף כלאי הכרם תופס את דמיו - אלמה תנן במתני': מכרן וקידש בדמיהם, מקודשת? אלמא אין אוסרין את דמיהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:6:1.english: So too, diverse kinds in a vineyard should transfer [their sanctity] to their proceeds - [If so,] why did we learn in the Mishnah: "If he sold them and betrothed [a woman] with their proceeds, she is betrothed"? Evidently, they do not render their proceeds forbidden.

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:7:1.hebrew: שהוא נבלה - הואיל וסקלו, ונבלה — כבר למדנו מ״לא תאכלו כל נבלה״ (דברים יד) שאסורה באכילה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:7:1.english: That it is a carcass - Since they stoned it, and regarding a carcass, we have already learned from “You shall not eat any carcass” (Deuteronomy 14:21) that it is forbidden to be eaten.

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:7:2.hebrew: מגיד דאם שחטו כו' - ותרתי אשמועינן קרא: "סקול יסקל השור", ואם נשחט — "לא יאכל":
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:7:2.english: [It] tells [you] that if one slaughtered it, etc. - And the verse teaches us two [things]: "The ox shall be stoned," and if it was slaughtered — "it shall not be eaten."

Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:9:1.hebrew: להיכא דסקליה מסקל - ולאסריה בהנאה אתא, ד״לא יאכל״ משמע איסורי הנאה כדרבי אבהו, דמנבילה נפקא לן בה איסור הנאה, שהנבלה פרט בה הכתוב היתר הנאה, ולהכי כתיב בדידיה בהדיא ״לא יאכל״ ולא פרט אחריו היתר. ו״בעל השור נקי״ לדרשא אחרינא אתא — לחצי כופר ודמי ולדות, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 56b:9:1.english: To [a case] where they stoned it - And it comes to prohibit [deriving] benefit from it, for “it shall not be eaten” implies a prohibition against deriving benefit, in accordance with [the statement of] Rabbi Abbahu; as from an animal carcass [neveilah] we derive a prohibition of benefit for it, since regarding an animal carcass Scripture specified permission of benefit, and therefore regarding this [ox] it is written explicitly: “It shall not be eaten,” and [Scripture] did not specify permission after it. And “the owner of the ox shall be clear” comes for another exposition — for [exemption from] half-ransom and the value of offspring, as [explained] below.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 56b:1:1.hebrew: כשברח - פי' ההיא ד"אין לוקחין עבדים":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 56b:1:1.english: "When he fled" - [This is an] explanation of that [mishnah] of "One may not purchase slaves."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 56b:1:2.hebrew: הא לא ברח קנסינן למוכר - כמו ההוא דלעיל דאמר "יחזרו דמים למקומם", שהוא קנסא למוכר שרוצה למכור בהמתו חוץ לירושלים — דקנס הוא כשתחזור לו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 56b:1:2.english: "Had he not fled, we would penalize the seller" - Like that [case] above, where [the Gemara] said, "The money shall return to its place," which is a penalty for the seller who wishes to sell his animal outside Jerusalem, for it is a penalty when it returns to him.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 56b:1:3.hebrew: ונקנסיה ללוקח - פירוש: שיאכל כנגדו בירושלים, ולא יתבטל. ולפירוש ר"מ פריך שפיר, שהמעות שביד המוכר יוצאין לחולין על ידי הלוקח. אבל לפי' ריב"א קשה: מאי פריך? אדרבה, מוטב לקנוס המוכר להוציא איסור מידו מלקנוס הלוקח וישאר האיסור ביד המוכר — כלומר, המעות שלא נתחללו, ושמא יאכלם חוץ לירושלים דכסבור נתחללו! וי"ל דלדידיה הכי פריך: וליקנסיה ללוקח שילך לבית המוכר ויאמר לו: "המעות שהן קדושין בידך תהא קדושתן על אלו", ואז יצאו לחולין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 56b:1:3.english: And let us penalize the buyer - Explanation: That he should eat [produce] corresponding to it in Jerusalem, and [the sale] should not be voided. And according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Meir, [the Gemara] asks well, for the money in the seller's possession becomes non-sacred through the buyer. However, according to the explanation of the Riva, it is difficult: What is [the Gemara] asking? On the contrary, it is better to penalize the seller to remove the prohibition from his possession, rather than to penalize the buyer and have the prohibition remain in the seller's possession — that is, the money that was not desacralized, and he might eat [i.e., spend] it outside Jerusalem, believing that it was desacralized! And one can say that according to his view, this is what [the Gemara] is asking: And let us penalize the buyer [by requiring] that he go to the seller's house and say to him: "The money that is sacred in your possession, let its sanctity be transferred onto these," and then it will become non-sacred.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 56b:2:1.hebrew: מסתברא כל היכא דאיכא איסור קנסינן ליה - פירוש: והיינו המוכר, שהרי המעות דמעשר ברשותו הוי קיימא, ולפיכך קנסו ליה שיחזרו דמים למקומם, והיינו שלא מכר בהמתו. וזה דוחק לפירוש ריב"א, דפירש דלעולם המעות שביד המוכר קדושים מקדושת מעשר וצריך להעלותן לירושלים; א"כ אדרבה, זכות הוא לו מהא דאמרן "יחזרו דמים למקומם", דטוב לו שיחזור לו בהמתו מלהעלות דמיו בירושלים! אבל לפירוש הר"ם ניחא. אך זה קשה לפירוש הקונטרס לעיל, דפי' גבי "אבל מתכוין להוציא מעות מעשר שני לחולין" דהמעות יצאו לחולין והבהמה קדושה, ועלה קאמר "יחזרו דמים למקומם"; ואם כן, לפי סברא זו הוי ליה למקנסיה ללוקח, למימר דיאכל כנגדו בירושלים, שהרי האיסור הוא בידו, דהיינו בהמה! אבל לפירוש [ריב"א] ניחא, שהרי האיסור הוא ביד המוכר. ואם תאמר: לעיל דקאמר גמרא דקנסוהו ללוקח ויאכל כנגדן, מאי קנס הוא זה? כי נמי אמר "יחזרו דמים למקומם", צריך הלוקח להעלות המעות לירושלים! וי"ל: דהקנס הוי מזה, דמסתמא לקח הבהמה ביוקר ממעות מעשר שני ליפטר עצמו מלעלות לירושלים, וכשנאמר לו שיאכל כנגדו בירושלים והמקח יהיה שלו — יהיה לו הפסד גדול בלקיחת הבהמה שלקח:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 56b:2:1.english: "It stands to reason that wherever the forbidden item is, there we penalize [him]" - Explanation: And this refers to the seller, for the ma'aser money remains in his possession, and therefore they penalized him that the money should return to its place, which means that [the sale is voided and retroactively] he did not sell his animal. And this is difficult according to the interpretation of Riva, who explained that the money in the seller's possession always remains consecrated with the sanctity of ma'aser and he must bring it up to Jerusalem. If so, on the contrary, it is an advantage for him that we say, "The money should return to its place," as it is better for him that his animal return to him than to bring up its value to Jerusalem! However, according to the interpretation of the Ram, it is well understood. Yet this is difficult according to the interpretation of Rashi above, who explained regarding [the baraita]: "However, if he intended to transfer ma'aser sheni coins to non-sacred status," that the coins go out to non-sacred status and the animal becomes consecrated, and concerning that [the Gemara] said, "The money should return to its place." And if so, according to this reasoning [that we penalize wherever the forbidden item is], they should have penalized the buyer by saying that he must eat its equivalent in Jerusalem, since the forbidden item is in his possession, namely the animal! But according to the interpretation of [Riva], it is well understood, for the forbidden item is in the seller's possession. And if you say: Above, where the Gemara states that they penalized the buyer and [ruled that] he must eat equivalent to them [in Jerusalem], what penalty is this? For even if it had said, "The money should return to its place," the buyer would still need to bring up the money to Jerusalem! And one can say that the penalty stems from this: that he presumably purchased the animal at an inflated price with ma'aser sheni money to exempt himself from going up to Jerusalem, and when we tell him that he must eat its equivalent in Jerusalem and the purchase will remain his, he will incur a great loss in the purchase of the animal that he bought.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 56b:3:1.hebrew: המקדש בערלה כו' אינה מקודשת - פירוש: לפי שאיסור הנאה. וא"ת: אמאי אינה מקודשת? הא שרי ליהנות ממנו שלא כדרך הנאתו, כדאמר בפ' כל שעה (פסחים דף כד:)! ויש לומר: בכאן מיירי דליכא שוה פרוטה אלא כדרך הנאתו. אי נמי יש לומר: דמיירי שפיר דאיכא שוה פרוטה אף שלא כדרך הנאתו; מ"מ, כיון שהאשה סבורה שיש לה ליהנות דרך הנאתן ואינו כן — לא סמכה דעתה, והוי מקח טעות. ואם תאמר: ואמאי לא חשיב בהך מתני' פיגול ונותר וטמא? ויש לומר: דבקדשים לא קא מיירי. והא דלא חשיב חמץ בפסח — משום דקסבר כרבי יוסי הגלילי, דשרי בהנאה בפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף כג.). והא דלא חשיב עבודת כוכבים — משום דלא שייך למיתני ביה "מכרן וקידש בדמיהן מקודשת", שהרי עבודת כוכבים תופסת דמיה; ושביעית אחר הביעור:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 56b:3:1.english: "One who betroths with orlah, etc., she is not betrothed" - Explanation: Because [these items are] prohibited for benefit. And if you say: Why is she not betrothed? Isn't it permitted to derive benefit from it in an atypical manner of its benefit, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 24b)? And one can say: Here we are dealing with [a case where] there is not the value of a perutah except through the typical manner of its benefit. Alternatively, one can say: It is dealing well [even in a case] where there is the value of a perutah even in an atypical manner of its benefit; nevertheless, since the woman assumes that she may derive benefit in their typical manner of benefit, and it is not so, her mind did not rely [on it], and it is a mistaken transaction. And if you say: And why did [the Tanna] not count in this Mishnah piggul, notar, and [sacrificial meat that became] ritually impure? And one can say: With consecrated items [the Tanna] is not dealing. And that which he did not count leaven on Passover — [it is] because he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who permits [leaven for] benefit, in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 23a). And that which he did not count idolatry — [it is] because it is not applicable to teach concerning it: "If he sold them and betrothed with their money, she is betrothed," for idolatry catches its money; and [likewise regarding produce of] the Sabbatical year after the removal [period].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 56b:4:1.hebrew: מנין שלא יצבע בו - אע"ג דאמרינן "לא יהנה", אצטריך לאשמועינן "שלא יצבע" — דס"ד דשרי, משום דחזותא לאו מילתא היא; ואיצטריך לאשמועינן "שלא ידליק" — דסלקא דעתך דשרי, משום דמכלה אותו. קמ"ל דאסור בכל ענין, וכדרך הנאתו; אבל שלא כדרך הנאתו — שרי. [וע"ע היטב תוס' ב"ק קא. ד"ה ולא יצבע]:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 56b:4:1.english: "From where [do we derive] that one may not dye with it" - Even though we say [that the verse implies that] one may not derive benefit [from it], it was necessary to inform us that one may not dye [with it], for it might enter your mind to say that it is permitted because appearance is of no substance; and it was necessary to inform us that one may not kindle [a lamp with it], for it might enter your mind to say that it is permitted because [burning] consumes it. [The verse therefore] teaches us that it is forbidden in every manner, [when done] in the normal manner of its benefit; but in an abnormal manner of its benefit, it is permitted. [And see further, carefully, Tosafot in Bava Kamma 101a, s.v. Velo yitzba].
